rv.q: All in all, the show bops along quite tastily.

The show, which the company bills as romantic-comedy-meets-horror, has its bright spots, particularly early on, but ultimately even strong performances and overall interesting and well-done staging can't really carry a rather aimless story that suffers from pacing problems.
This play—easily one of the best of the year—has everything.
Chemistry, comedy, and a little bloodlust make for an irresistible evening.
With heart, fun, and a touch of horror, The Untitled Vampire Play is an event that you will not want to miss.
By the poignant conclusion, we see something richer and more mournful at work that offers a metaphorical stake to our hearts.
It’s just plain bloody good fun!
Douglas's Untitled Vampire Play showcases the remarkable talent and serves as a powerful testament to this playwright's potential, suggesting a promising future.
Untitled Vampire Play is creative and visually arresting.
This play is chock full of modern and pop culture vampire lore rendering it canon as a very fun 2 hours steeped in mythology and relationship dynamics.
This is a play to sink your teeth into.
For something quite different and entertaining in theater, I would highly recommend Untitled Vampire Play at Lookingglass Theater.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this bloody rom-com, praising its charm, chemistry, and visual invention. One dissenter finds it uneven, but most agree Lookingglass's vampire love story delivers fun, if not immortal, theater.
